function: PG-PDQN jointly picks AP power, channel blocklength, and continuous RIS phase shifts to maximize delay determinacy, the probability that delay falls in a time window (p. 8-9).
system: Downlink, single-antenna AP, one passive reflecting RIS with 64 elements, K users with scalar channels, blocked direct LoS, 5.9 GHz carrier (p. 3, 11).
method: Multi-agent parameterized DQN (PG-PDQN): deterministic policy network for continuous RIS phases plus discrete Q-network, reinforcement learning; offline pretraining and online adjustment claimed (p. 9-11).
data_channel: Custom Python simulator: Rayleigh direct link, Rician RIS links (K = 3, also 6), distance-based path loss; no 3GPP model or measured data (p. 3-4, 11-13).
test_conditions: One simulated layout (users within a 10 m circle); training curves for sweeps of delay limits, Pmax, nmax, Rician factor (3, 6) and learning rate (p. 11-13).
baselines: Fixed-phase, equalized-power and equalized-blocklength strategies (Fig. 8); learned DQN, Dueling DQN and DDPG on the same problem (Fig. 9-10) (p. 12-13).
metrics: Delay determinacy (probability delay falls in the window), shown as average reward versus training steps; convergence of reward (p. 9, 11-13).
complexity: none; only an estimated decision time under 0.001 ms, cited from [35], not measured (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 11: "We refer to [32] for the simulation setup on the Python platform". Channels are Rayleigh (direct) and Rician (RIS) with distance path loss (p. 3-4); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is cited.
q2_support: p. 12-13: Figs. 6-11, and Fig. 9 versus Fig. 10 (Rician factor 3 versus 6), are separate training curves per setting; no trained policy is tested on an unseen scenario. p. 11 only claims "combines offline pretraining and online adjustment" without an experiment.
q3_support: p. 12: "the agent in the DDGS strategy achieves higher reward values than the fixed phase shift strategy" (fixed RIS configuration). p. 12: "The DQN and Dueling DQN [44] algorithms have to discretize the continuous actions", plus DDPG [45], compared on the same reward (Fig. 9-10), which is the delay determinacy (Eq. 43, p. 9).
q4_support: p. 11: "The total time consuming is estimated to be less than 0.001 ms [35]". This is an estimate taken from [35], not measured here; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count, or measured runtime is given, only the qualitative "reduces the algorithm complexity".
q5_support: p. 11: "We refer to [32] for the simulation setup on the Python platform". No code or data link is given and no dataset is used; the channels are simulated.
notes: Area 3: the learned PG-PDQN outputs the RIS phase shifts (continuous action, p. 9) jointly with AP power and blocklength, so the learning acts on physical-layer variables; delay determinacy is derived analytically with stochastic network calculus (p. 5-7). One antenna at the AP but a RIS is present, so the system check passes. q3 judgment call for the reviewer: the non-learned side is the fixed-phase strategy (a fixed RIS configuration) and the equalized power and blocklength strategies, which still use DRL for the other variables (p. 12); the learned side is DQN, Dueling DQN and DDPG. q4 is borderline: the only runtime figure is an estimate cited from [35], so I mark it 0.
